features.claim: Giganotosaurus was a very large meat-eating dinosaur.
features.quote: Giganotosaurus was a very large meat-eating dinosaur that lived in prehistoric South America.
Though incompletely known, the skull of Giganotosaurus appears to have been low.

features.claim: Its teeth were long, blade-like and serrated, good for slicing.
features.quote: long, blade-like and serrated, ideal for slicing

features.claim: Its teeth were compressed sideways and had serrations.
features.quote: The teeth were compressed sideways and had serrations.
The neck was strong and the pectoral girdle proportionally small.

features.claim: Its shoulder girdle was small compared with its body.
features.quote: The neck was strong and the pectoral girdle proportionally small.

features.claim: The front of its lower jaw was flattened and had a downward-pointing chin at the tip.
features.quote: The front of the lower jaw was flattened and had a downward-projecting process (or "chin") at the tip.

features.claim: It had rough, wrinkled nasal bones and a ridge-like crest on the bone in front of the eye.
features.quote: The skull was low, with rugose (rough and wrinkled) nasal bones and a ridge-like crest on the lacrimal bone in front of the eye.

features.claim: It was probably longer but more lightly built than the bulkier and heavier Tyrannosaurus rex.
features.quote: At around 13 metres long, it was probably longer but more lightly built than the bulkier and heavier Tyrannosaurus rex.

not_this.claim: Old pictures that show the skulls of these dinosaurs as too long are wrong.
not_this.quote: In 2010, the paleontologist Gregory S. Paul suggested that the skulls of carcharodontosaurs had been reconstructed as too long in general.

not_this.claim: The largest size estimates for Giganotosaurus are considered exaggerated by some writers.
not_this.quote: Some writers have considered the largest size estimates for both specimens exaggerated.

debated.claim: It is not known for sure whether Giganotosaurus was larger than Tyrannosaurus.
debated.quote: It is therefore impossible to determine with certainty whether it was larger than Tyrannosaurus, for example, which has been considered the largest theropod historically.

debated.claim: The exact size of Giganotosaurus is hard to determine because the remains found so far are incomplete.
debated.quote: Giganotosaurus was one of the largest known terrestrial carnivores, but the exact size has been hard to determine due to the incompleteness of the remains found so far.

debated.claim: Scientists have not yet found a complete Giganotosaurus specimen, so some of its skeleton is still unknown.
debated.quote: Scientists haven’t yet discovered a complete Giganotosaurus specimen. Some of the skeleton is still unknown.

second_reading.claim: It had very strong jaws and could deliver a powerful bite.
second_reading.quote: Either way, Giganotosaurus had very strong jaws and could certainly deliver a powerful bite.
second_reading.why: a picture could not show it

second_reading.claim: The idea that its large size let it run fast is wrong; its long limbs would have limited it to walking.
second_reading.quote: The relatively long limbs, which were long argued to indicate good running ability, would instead have mechanically limited it to walking gaits, and it would therefore not have been a high-speed pursuit predator.
second_reading.why: a picture could not show it

second_reading.claim: Experts are not sure what Giganotosaurus hunted.
second_reading.quote: But experts aren’t sure what it hunted.
second_reading.why: a picture could not show it
